newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act says Labour, NZ First plotting death of ECA.
newsitem.headline: Act says Labour, NZ First plotting death of ECA.

text.p: Act New Zealand finance spokesman Rodney Hide said on Tuesday that Labour's coalition proposal to New Zealand First would spell the end of the Employment Contracts Act.

"The Labour and New Zealand First heads of agreement on labour relations, we understand from a very good source, is good faith bargaining and ratifying all the provisions of the ILO (International Labour Organisation) -- essentially the death of the ECA," Hide told reporters.
He said his details of the agreement came from a source very close to Labour.
Asked about the ramifications, Hide said: "It means Winston (Peters) has to go with National because it's so wacky, and even NZ First concedes it is wacky."
Hide said NZ First campaigned on keeping the ECA but making some amendments. "This is not making some amendments, this is its total destruction."
ILO conventions would allow strikes covering multi-employer contracts. At the moment only single-site or single-employer strikes are lawful.
A Labour party source confirmed the ECA was covered in some detail in the coalition proposal to NZ First, with references to good faith bargaining and ILO principles.

Labour fought the election on promises to repeal the 1991 ECA and replace it with an Employment Relations Act. It said it would apply ILO principles of free worker association and collective bargaining, but workers would have the right to sign individual contracts.
